To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-terminal part, but not the central, modulator domain of the inositol-1,4, 5-triphosphate (IP(3))-receptor harbors two distinct binding sites for Bcl- 2 proteins.

the Bcl- 2/Bcl-X binding site in the C terminal domain of the type-1 IP3 receptor is composed of elements preceding the cytosolic tail of the sixth transmembranal domain, and the Bcl-X binding site on the modulatory domain is composed of elements located in a region between the N terminal domain and the central helical domain.

IP(3)Rs contain two binding sites for antiapoptotic Bcl-XL and Bcl- 2 proteins, and that Bcl-XL binds with higher affinity than Bcl-2 to the IP( 3)R C-terminus, whereas the opposite holds true for the IP(3 )R central domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the binding sites on the IP(3R) for the anti-apoptosis proteins Bcl-2 family.
the molecular basis for the interaction between the Bcl- 2 family and IP(3) receptors, which is of importance for the regulation of intracellular calcium homeostasis.
the molecular mechanisms of the anti-apopotic protein Bcl-2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bcl- 2-binding site on the IP(3 )R1 is composed of at least two distinct sites: the central modulatory domain and a second site in the C terminal part of the IP3R1, near the Ca(+) channel pore.
the C-terminal site is the major site for binding of Bcl-X(L), while the central site is the major one for Bcl- 2.
Bcl-2 binds the IP(3)-binding site in the modulatory domain, whereas Bcl-X(L)/Mcl-1 preferentially bind to the C-terminal domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal site is the major one, while the modulatory domain site is the minor one.
Bcl-2 can bind to two different domains of the IP3R, whereas Bcl-XL can bind to the C-terminal region only.
the Bcl-X(L)-IP(3) interaction is mainly mediated through the C-terminal domain, while the Bcl- 2-IP(3) receptor interaction involves both the central and C-terminal domain of IP( 3) receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bcl- 2/Bcl-X binding sites in the C-terminal region of the IP( 3)R are not the same for both Bcl- 1 and Bcl-X, and that Bcl-X(L), but not Bcl-2 binds to the central, C2B, domain of the IP3R.
Bcl-2 binds both sites, whereas Bcl-X(L), which has a lower affinity for the C-terminal domain, binds only to the C-terminal domain.
Bcl-X(L), in contrast to Bcl-2 or Bcl-X(S), binds preferentially to the C-terminal domain.
